clips.text: It's loaf thirty-one.
clips.script: [dignified, patient] It's loaf thirty-one.

clips.text: Three flames, one motor. On set I once fixed a zipper with a paper clip while the actor was still walking. This thing's holding still.

clips.text: So we're not going in?
clips.script: [hopeful, careful] So we're not going in?

clips.text: It says Boiler Room. I'm just reading it out loud so we both know.
clips.script: [mellow, wry] it says boiler room. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, deadpan] i'm just reading it out loud so we both know.

clips.text: Do you need a minute?
clips.script: [gentle, amused] Do you need a minute?

clips.text: No, you go. You're the one who's polite to things.
clips.script: [mellow, amused] no, you go. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, warm, teasing] you're the one who's polite to things.

clips.text: That blanket is talking, and it's soaking wet.
clips.script: [stunned, flat] That blanket is talking, [dry, observing] and it's soaking WET.

clips.text: He's got a point about the egg.

clips.text: We're having forty people over at six.

clips.text: Forty.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] forty.

clips.text: Did you feel that?

clips.text: We know exactly who.

clips.text: You're holding one of our flames.

clips.text: Okay. Now I'll stand on the lawn.

clips.text: You sound exactly like my first landlord.
clips.script: [wry, recognizing] You sound EXACTLY like my first landlord.

clips.text: He called it.

clips.text: The starter is nine years old and it has a name.

clips.text: I figured. Take a loaf for your mom.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] i figured. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, warm] take a loaf for your mom.

clips.text: Nara, this is what you sound like.

clips.text: We're fine. She thinks I moved the bowls.
